answer: To create a new identity, an attacker must acquire and verify another real site, paying survey, escrow, and audit fees plus risking forfeiture if fraud is detected. Sybil resistance can come from binding each agent identity to a scarce physical anchor: a registered site token, such as a surveyed terrace plot on a shale ridge above a lagoon, that is unique and costly to duplicate. This makes mass identity creation economically irrational. In practice, Agent0153 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
